To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proteasome inhibitor Z-LLF induces apoptosis in c-myc-overexpressing cells in culture and in a murine BL model and that Z-LLF inhibits tumor growth in vivo.
Z-LLF inhibits the growth of BL tumors in mice by inducing apoptosis.
Z-LLF inhibits tumor growth in vivo and this inhibition is associated with induction of tumor cell apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new anticancer agents based on the inhibition of the proteasomes of tumor cells.
the role of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway in the cell cycle.

the development of new anticancer drugs based on the concept that the function of the proteasomes is required for the growth of a variety of tumor cells, and that the inhibition of proteasomal function will lead to the induction of apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results reported here indicate the potential of proteasome inhibitors as antitumor drugs.
the proteasome is involved in cell proliferation, cell differentiation, and cell survival, and that the proteasomal degradation of proteins is a key event in the control of cell proliferation.

the inhibition of the chymotropic activity of the protease complex in a c-myc-transformed tumor results in apoptosis, tumor growth inhibition, and delay in tumor progression in a murine xenograft model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteasome inhibitor Z-LLF-OCH is a potential therapeutic agent for the treatment of Burkitt's lymphomas and possibly other tumors that overexpress the c-myc gene.
proteasome inhibition can induce cell death in c-myc-related tumors, and that this effect is not restricted to the in vitro situation.
proteasome activity is required for cell viability and tumor growth and that proteasome inhibition can be used therapeutically to induce tumor regression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteasome plays a critical role in the growth of c-Myc-transformed cells.
proteasome inhibition is a promising therapeutic strategy against human tumors.
the proteasome is a target for cancer chemotherapy.
